key_insight: Capping CsPbBr3 perovskite films with few-layer hBN dramatically improves heat dissipation without changing the film’s optical behavior.
engineering_relevance: The hBN/perovskite heterostructure offers a practical route to making perovskite optoelectronic and solar devices more thermally robust under high-power operation.
method: Built planar hot-pressed CsPbBr3 thin films
Integrated few-layer hBN using a large-scale semidry transfer process
Compared uncapped vs hBN-capped films with microscopy, spectroscopy, and heat-diffusion simulations
evidence_signal: The heterostructure reached a measured thermal conductivity of about 3 W/(m·K), roughly 7× higher than bare CsPbBr3 films at 0.45 W/(m·K), and showed reduced laser-induced heating under continuous-wave excitation.
watch_item: Scalability and long-term interface stability of the hBN capping layer in real device stacks still need validation under operational stress.
paper_title: Improved Heat Dissipation in CsPbBr${_3}$-hBN Heterostructures
